name: gitflipper
description: Automatically switch Git identities (name, email, SSH key) based on workspace directory.

gitFlip.profiles.markdownDescription:
Your Git identity profiles. Each profile stores a **name**, **email**, and optionally an **SSH key** and **directory rules**.

Example:
```json
[
  {
    "name": "Work",
    "email": "you@company.com",
    "userName": "Your Name",
    "sshKeyPath": "~/.ssh/id_work",
    "directories": ["~/work"]
  }
]
```

Use the command **GitFlipper: Create Profile** for a guided setup wizard.

name.markdownDescription: A display name for this profile (e.g., `Work`, `Personal`, `Open Source`). This appears in the status bar and command palette.

email.markdownDescription: The email address that will appear on your Git commits. Make sure this matches what your Git hosting service expects (e.g., your GitHub or Bitbucket account email).

userName.markdownDescription: The name that will appear on your Git commits (e.g., `Jane Doe`). This is your display name, not your username.

sshKeyPath.markdownDescription:
Path to the **private** SSH key file for this profile (e.g., `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work`). This is the file **without** the `.pub` extension.

SSH keys are used to authenticate with remote Git servers like GitHub or Bitbucket. If you're not sure what this is, you can leave it empty.

directories.markdownDescription:
Directories where this profile should automatically activate. When you open a project inside any of these directories, GitFlipper will set this profile's identity.

Example: Setting `~/work` will match `~/work/project-a`, `~/work/project-b`, etc.

If multiple profiles match, the most specific (longest) path wins.

gitFlip.defaultProfile.markdownDescription:
The profile to use when no directory rule matches the current workspace. Set this to the name of one of your profiles (e.g., `Personal`).

Leave empty to show a warning when no profile matches.

gitFlip.warnOnMismatch.markdownDescription: Show a notification when GitFlipper detects that the repo's current identity is different from the expected profile. This helps catch cases where your identity was changed manually or by another tool.

gitFlip.autoSwitch.markdownDescription:
Automatically apply the matching profile when you open a workspace. When enabled, GitFlipper writes `user.name` and `user.email` to the repo's local Git config.

Disable this if you prefer to switch profiles manually using the **GitFlipper: Switch Profile** command.

gitFlip.sshStrategy.markdownDescription:
How GitFlipper applies SSH keys:

- **`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`** (recommended) — Sets an environment variable in VS Code's terminal. Safe, scoped to VS Code, no side effects on other apps.
- **`ssh-agent`** — Adds/removes keys from your system's SSH agent. Works system-wide but affects all terminal sessions, not just VS Code.
